text: 아이템 목록 API(backend/app/api/routes/items.py의 `GET /api/v1/items/`)에 region 필터 추가해줘. backend/app/models.py의 Item에 `region` 필드 넣고(Alembic 마이그레이션 포함), 쿼리 파라미터로 `preferred_regions` 받게 해줘. 해당 region에서 결과가 하나도 없으면 인접 region까지 범위 넓혀서 다시 조회하는 로직도 같이 부탁해.

Add ETag and If-None-Match support to the item endpoints in backend/app/api/routes/items.py (`GET /api/v1/items/` and `GET /api/v1/items/{id}`) so the frontend stops re-downloading unchanged items. Don't add any new dependencies; compute the ETag from the item's id, title, description and created_at with the standard library (hashlib), and return 304 with no body when it matches.

Some users want items to lock after a while. Can you add an optional `edit_window_minutes` to the Item model in backend/app/models.py (with an Alembic migration), use the item's existing `created_at` as the start time, and have `update_item` in backend/app/api/routes/items.py reject edits that arrive after the window plus a 30-second grace period?

`backend/app/api/routes/items.py`에서 `created_at` 날짜로 아이템을 필터링할 때 UTC 자정 기준으로 날짜를 잘라서 KST 기준으로 하루 경계가 9시간 밀리고 있어요. 그래서 오전 9시 전에 만든 아이템이 전날로 잡히는데, 요청한 timezone 기준으로 날짜 자르도록 고쳐주고 `backend/tests/api/routes/test_items.py`에 `pytest.mark.parametrize`로 테이블 테스트도 추가해 주세요.

The items API returns a 500 on `GET /api/v1/items/` when the current user has zero items, because `read_items` in backend/app/api/routes/items.py assumes the result list is non-empty. Fix it and keep it backward compatible: an empty list should come back as `{"data": [], "count": 0}` with 200, the same `ItemsPublic` shape the frontend already parses, not a 404 or null.

Our backend deadlocks under load. In backend/app/api/routes/users.py, `create_user` keeps the DB transaction (and its row locks) open while it calls `send_email` from backend/app/utils.py over SMTP, and `delete_user` locks the item rows and the user row in the opposite order from `update_user`. Can you restructure it so we never hold a lock across the email call and the lock order is consistent?

Item and user created dates show the wrong day for people in Australia. `created_at` in backend/app/models.py ends up serialized as a naive datetime in `ItemPublic`/`UserPublic`, so it gets interpreted in the server/client local timezone and shifts by a day. Please fix it so it stays a timezone-aware UTC datetime end to end and add a test in backend/tests/ that runs with `TZ=Australia/Sydney`.

Goal: break `backend/app/models.py` into an `app/models/` package.
- New `app/models/dtos.py` for the Pydantic request/response models (`UserCreate`, `ItemPublic`, `Token`, etc.), with no `table=True` models in it
- New `app/models/user.py` and `app/models/item.py` for the `User` and `Item` table models
- `app/models/__init__.py` re-exports the public API, so existing `from app.models import ...` in `crud.py`, the routes and `alembic/env.py` work with no changes
- No circular imports between the modules
Acceptance: `bash backend/scripts/test.sh` and `bash backend/scripts/lint.sh` pass, and `alembic revision --autogenerate` detects no database structure changes.

Our items page (`frontend/src/routes/_layout/items.tsx`) and the `AddItem`, `EditItem` and `DeleteItem` components in `frontend/src/components/Items/` call `ItemsService` directly and handle the query cache invalidation themselves. Could you move that into a `frontend/src/hooks/useItems.ts` hook, so the components only deal with UI state and the page looks and behaves the same?
`backend/app/utils.py`의 `generate_password_reset_token`/`verify_password_reset_token`에 대해 pytest 테스트 추가해줘. 만료 시간 전에는 토큰이 이메일을 돌려주는지, 만료 시간 지나면 `None`이 나오는지 확인하고, 시간은 `monkeypatch`로 현재 시각을 고정해서 제어해줘.

Add tests under `backend/tests/` (e.g. a new `backend/tests/test_email_rendering.py`) for the email rendering in `backend/app/utils.py` (the main email-rendering function and the `generate_*_email` helpers). Cover the new account email, the reset password link, and HTML being escaped when a username or project name contains markup. Keep the diff minimal: don't add any dependencies to `backend/pyproject.toml` and don't change the public API of `app/utils.py`. Reuse the existing fixtures in `backend/tests/conftest.py` and the helpers in `backend/tests/utils/`.

프론트엔드 Items 페이지(`frontend/src/routes/_layout/items.tsx`, `frontend/src/components/Items/AddItem.tsx`)의 오프라인 동작 테스트를 작성해줘. 기존 Playwright 설정(`frontend/playwright.config.ts`, `frontend/tests/auth.setup.ts`)을 쓰고, `frontend/tests/items.spec.ts`에 케이스를 추가해줘. 네트워크가 끊긴 상태에서 아이템을 여러 개 추가했다가 다시 연결되면 TanStack Query가 순서대로 요청을 보내고 목록에 그 순서대로 나타나는지 확인해줘. 네트워크는 `context.setOffline()`이랑 `page.route()`로 mock 처리하면 돼.
docstrings for backend/app/api/deps.py, reviewer flagged missing raises: section on get_current_user (403/404 httpexception)

백엔드(`backend/Dockerfile`) k8s 배포용 차트 패키지 만들어줘. 위치는 새로 `deploy/chart/backend/` 아래에 두고. liveness랑 readiness 헬스 체크는 `backend/app/api/routes/utils.py`의 `/api/v1/utils/health-check/` 엔드포인트에 연결하고, 지금 Dockerfile에 `--workers 4`로 고정돼 있는 uvicorn worker 수를 컨테이너 memory limit 기준으로 잡히게 해줘. 지금 아이템 API 서비스가 OOMKilled 계속 나서 급해.

Goal: zero-downtime deploys for the FastAPI backend (`backend/app/main.py`) on our k3s cluster.
- Handle SIGTERM via the app lifespan in `backend/app/main.py`: stop accepting new requests, drain in-flight requests for up to 25s (`--timeout-graceful-shutdown 25` in `backend/Dockerfile`), then exit
- Set `terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30` and a `preStop` sleep of 5s in a new `deploy/k8s/backend.yaml`
- Add a readiness endpoint `/api/v1/utils/readyz` in `backend/app/api/routes/utils.py` that flips to 503 as soon as shutdown begins
- RollingUpdate with `maxUnavailable: 0`, `maxSurge: 1`
Acceptance: during a rollout under a load script in a new `scripts/loadgen/` that hammers `POST /api/v1/items/`, zero item writes are dropped (the script's count of 5xx/connection errors stays at 0).

Deploy the FastAPI backend (`backend/`) to the three regional VMs, security first: the systemd unit should run as a dedicated non-root user with `ProtectSystem=strict`, `NoNewPrivileges=yes`, and `SECRET_KEY` loaded via `LoadCredential=` instead of an env var (have `backend/app/core/config.py` read it from `$CREDENTIALS_DIRECTORY`). Add the unit and an Ansible playbook under `deploy/ansible/`.

Our FastAPI backend keeps failing the first health check (`/api/v1/utils/health-check/`) after deploy on Cloud Run because startup takes ~9s (`scripts/prestart.sh` plus import time). Can you add a startup check config, turn on CPU boost, and see if precompiling bytecode in `backend/Dockerfile` (`UV_COMPILE_BYTECODE=1`) gets cold start under 4s?

We need to ship the backend to FastAPI Cloud (there's already a `.fastapicloudignore`). Can you set up the deploy step with the deploy token from CI secrets, and make production deploys use `ENVIRONMENT=production` and a real `SECRET_KEY` and `FIRST_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD` instead of the local `.env` defaults (`changethis`) they're accidentally using now?

Add an export in a new `backend/app/export.py` that dumps one day of items (by `created_at`, ~40M rows) from the database into parquet files partitioned by `owner_id`. It has to run on the 512MB worker pod, so read with a server-side cursor in chunks (`yield_per` on the SQLModel session) and write row groups incrementally; never load the full day into memory. Please check heap usage with a test run on staging's 2026-10-15 data before calling it done.

Goal: bulk-import items from partner CSVs into the database.
- New module `backend/app/importer.py`, using the stdlib `csv` module and the existing SQLModel `Item` model in `backend/app/models.py`
- Input columns: owner_email, created_at, title, quality_flag; files can be up to 2GB
- Skip rows with quality_flag = 'E' but count them and log the count per file
- Convert created_at from the partner's local time (America/Chicago) to UTC, handling the DST fallback hour without dropping rows
- Insert in batches of 50k rows
Acceptance: a sample file in a new `backend/tests/fixtures/items_2026_03.csv` loads with the expected 2,976 items per owner for March, and re-importing the same file doesn't create duplicates (add a unique constraint on owner_id + created_at via an Alembic migration in `backend/app/alembic/versions/` and use ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING).

We need to hand item history from the app to a university research group. Add an anonymizing export in a new backend/app/export.py, plus a route in backend/app/api/routes/items.py. It should replace owner_id with a salted hash, bucket created_at into month ranges, and drop the free-text description. Do a security-first pass: the salt comes from Settings in backend/app/core/config.py and is never logged, the output has no column that can be joined back to users, and there's a test in backend/tests/api/routes/test_items.py asserting that.
백엔드의 아이템 클릭률 예측 서빙 코드(`backend/app/ml/ctr.py`)에서 피처 해싱 버킷 수가 학습 때랑 달라서 예측값이 다 0.5 근처로 나와요. 학습 config에서 버킷 수를 읽어오도록 바꾸고, 불일치하면 `backend/app/main.py` 시작 시점에 에러가 나게 해주세요.

Goal: serve the voice keyword-spotting model from the FastAPI backend.
- Load `backend/models/kws_int8.onnx` with onnxruntime once at startup (lifespan in `backend/app/main.py`)
- Expose `async def detect(samples: np.ndarray) -> Keyword | None` in a new `backend/app/kws/__init__.py`, plus a POST route in a new `backend/app/api/routes/kws.py` registered in `backend/app/api/main.py`
- Compute log-mel features with numpy only (40 bins, 25ms window, 10ms hop) in `backend/app/kws/features.py`, matching the training reference exactly
- Add a parity test in `backend/tests/kws/test_features.py` comparing against fixtures in `backend/tests/fixtures/mel_*.npy` (max abs diff < 1e-4)
Constraints: no librosa/torch at runtime, the backend Docker image grows by under 30MB, inference under 15ms per 1s clip on a Raspberry Pi 4.

The item pricing model we retrain nightly in `backend/app/ml/train.py` has no record of which training run produced the model in prod. Can you write the metrics and dataset hash into a `model_metadata.json` next to the artifact and expose it at `/api/v1/utils/model-info` in `backend/app/api/routes/utils.py`?

Goal: add an item risk classifier to the backend.
- New package `backend/app/ml/` that loads an XGBoost model from S3 at startup (path from a new `RISK_MODEL_URI` setting in `backend/app/core/config.py`)
- `predict(item: Item) -> RiskPrediction` returning LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH with probability
- Feature extraction in `backend/app/ml/features.py` must match the training notebook column order; add a unit test against `backend/tests/fixtures/golden_features.csv`
- Hot-reload the model when a new version lands without restarting the container
- Record a `risk_predict_latency` timing metric
Acceptance: `backend/scripts/test.sh` passes and prediction stays under 5ms p95 in a benchmark.
`pages/users/[id].tsx`에서 TensorFlow.js로 사용자 프로필 사진 분류 모델을 돌리는데, Safari에서만 결과가 이상하게 나와요. 전처리에서 RGB/BGR 순서나 정규화가 브라우저별로 다른지 확인하고 `utils/preprocess.ts` 고쳐주세요.

Add a personalized next-item suggestion to the items page, using a small model trained in the browser on the user's own item history. Put it in a new `frontend/src/components/Items/ItemSuggester.tsx` and render it from `frontend/src/routes/_layout/items.tsx`. Privacy first: all training and inference stays on device, nothing about the user's history goes to our API or analytics, and the model file lives in the browser's origin-scoped IndexedDB.
are /docs and openapi.json exposed in prod? check openapi_url in backend/app/main.py and ENVIRONMENT in backend/app/core/config.py

Our email rendering (the email-rendering function in backend/app/utils.py) fills the HTML files in backend/app/email-templates/ with user-supplied values like full name and email, and I suspect it does that without autoescaping, so HTML injection is possible. Plan before coding: list every Jinja rendering site in the backend and the risk for each first, then wait for my go-ahead before enabling autoescape and escaping user input.

The frontend keeps the access token in localStorage (see frontend/src/hooks/useAuth.ts and frontend/src/main.tsx), and BACKEND_CORS_ORIGINS in .env still has some wide-open origins left over from old debugging. Can you move the token to an httpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict cookie set by backend/app/api/routes/login.py and read in backend/app/api/deps.py, and tighten CORS to only the domains we actually need?

프론트엔드 아이템 목록(frontend/src/components/Items/columns.tsx)에서 판매자가 description에 넣은 임의 URL을 그대로 링크로 열고 있어. 그런데 frontend/src/hooks/useAuth.ts는 access_token을 localStorage에 두고 있어서 열린 페이지에서 토큰에 접근할 수 있는지 걱정돼. 허용 도메인만 열리도록 막고, 토큰이 노출되는 범위도 검토해줘.

Speed up `GET /api/v1/items/` in `backend/app/api/routes/items.py` for superusers, who use it for the analytics export.
- Right now a superuser listing over ~200k items runs the count query and the page query one after the other, loads full `Item` rows, and takes several seconds per page.
- Select only the columns `ItemPublic` needs instead of loading whole ORM objects.
- Add an index on `item.owner_id` with a new Alembic migration in `backend/app/alembic/versions/`, so the non-superuser filter stops doing a sequential scan.
- Avoid building an intermediate list per row; return the page straight from the query result.
Acceptance: responses identical to the current ones for the cases in `backend/tests/api/routes/test_items.py`, p95 under 300ms on a seeded 200k-item database, and a benchmark test added for the listing query.

Our backend container takes ~90s to come up under `compose.yml`, so the healthcheck regularly fails during deploys. Can you figure out what's slow at startup? I suspect `backend/scripts/prestart.sh` (the DB wait plus the Alembic upgrade) and `init_db` in `backend/app/core/db.py` / `backend/app/initial_data.py`. Get it under 30s, for example by skipping or deferring the non-critical setup.

The items page (`frontend/src/routes/_layout/items.tsx`, rendered through `Common/DataTable.tsx` with `Items/columns.tsx`) is just a long table right now. Could you turn it into a grid of cards showing title, description and created time, with items older than 30 days visibly greyed out?

The user settings page in `frontend/src/routes/_layout/settings.tsx` needs a proper tabbed layout: tabs for account info (`UserSettings/UserInformation.tsx`), password (`UserSettings/ChangePassword.tsx`), and appearance (`Common/Appearance.tsx`), with `DeleteAccount` in its own danger-zone section. Plan before coding: propose the component layout and any route/state changes first, and wait for my OK before touching the mutations or `useAuth.ts`.
관리자 화면의 사용자 추가 다이얼로그(`frontend/src/components/Admin/AddUser.tsx`)에 필드가 한 번에 다 나와서 관리자들이 중간에 자주 포기해요. 단계별 입력(기본정보 → 비밀번호 → 권한 설정)으로 나누고, 상단에 진행 단계 표시를 넣어주세요.

The admin users page (`frontend/src/routes/_layout/admin.tsx` with `components/Admin/columns.tsx`) feels flat. Can you add filter chips at the top (All / Superusers / Regular users), show an initials avatar on each user row, and make inactive users look clearly disabled?

Add a nightly retraining job to the backend. It should retrain a scikit-learn spam classifier on the last 30 days of `Item` rows (by `created_at`), compare AUC against the current model, and only swap the new one into a model registry (a new `backend/app/ml/registry.py`) if it improves by at least 0.5%. Plan before coding: write up the steps, where the job lives and how the swap stays atomic, then wait for my OK.

Rewrite `README.md` for this app. Cover install, running the dev server, the `/users` and `/users/[id]` pages, and the `GET /api/users` route, with example output for each (rendered page and JSON from `utils/sample-data.ts`). Accessibility first: use properly ordered headings, alt text on every screenshot, and don't rely on color alone in the sample terminal output.

The email-rendering function in `backend/app/utils.py` re-reads and recompiles the Jinja file from `backend/app/email-templates/` on every send. A batch of ~400 new-account and password-reset emails takes about 9s and a lot of memory. Cache the compiled Jinja objects and reuse them across sends. Visual polish first: `new_account.html` and `reset_password.html` must render exactly as they do now.
